children: By Hernan Nessi and Fabiola Arámburo

Argentina's monthly inflation rate slowed to 1.7% in August, official data showed on Thursday, as easing food-price pressures helped extend a run of lower readings under libertarian President Javier Milei.
The August figure matched analysts' expectations in a Reuters poll and was the lowest monthly reading since May 2025, when consumer prices rose 1.5%.
Annual inflation eased to 33.5% in August from 33.8% in July, according to national statistics agency INDEC, with the figure also nearly in line with analysts' forecasts.

The biggest monthly increases were in housing, water, electricity, gas and other fuels, which rose 2.8%, and education, up 2.5%. Food and non-alcoholic beverages, the largest component of the index, rose 1.7%.

Analysts had predicted that softer food inflation likely helped drive the monthly slowdown, offering some relief to households, though it may add to pressure on companies already contending with weak demand.
Analysts polled by Argentina's central bank expect inflation to end the year at 30%, with the economy growing 2.1%.
